    - heading "One receptor family, two very different molecules." [level=2]
    - complementary "Regulatory status":
      - generic "Regulatory status by country (6)" [active]
      - term: United Kingdom
      - definition:
        - text: In the UK, afamelanotide is licensed under exceptional circumstances and prescribed only in specialist porphyria centres, and NICE did not recommend it for NHS use (July 2023).
        - generic: "Source: Afamelanotide for treating erythropoietic protoporphyria (NICE highly specialised technologies guidance HST27)"
      - term: European Union
      - definition:
        - text: In the EU, afamelanotide (Scenesse implant) is authorised for erythropoietic protoporphyria, under exceptional circumstances (European Commission, 22 December 2014), and is prescribed only by specialists in recognised EPP centres.
        - generic: "Source: Scenesse (afamelanotide) — European public assessment report (EPAR) · Union Register of medicinal products for human use (authorised, not active and refused lists)"
      - term: Portugal
      - definition:
        - text: In Portugal, Scenesse is authorised through the EU procedure but classified as a restricted-prescription medicine for exclusive hospital use (MSRM restrita, alínea a), and no presentation is marketed in Portugal (INFARMED's Infomed register, 25 September 2026).
        - generic: "Source: Infomed – base de dados de medicamentos do Infarmed (pesquisa avançada and 'Detalhes do Medicamento' pages) · Decreto-Lei n.º 176/2006, de 30 de agosto – Estatuto do Medicamento (regime jurídico dos medicamentos de uso humano), versão consolidada"
      - term: Brazil
      - definition:
        - text: "In Brazil, no registered medicine containing afamelanotide (Scenesse) was found: ANVISA's open-data register and its online medicines search returned no match on 25 September 2026, and the substance is absent from ANVISA's substance dictionary."
        - generic: "Source: Dados abertos de medicamentos registrados (DADOS_ABERTOS_MEDICAMENTOS.csv) · Documentação e Dicionário de Dados – Registros Válidos Medicamento V1 · Consultas – Medicamentos (product and substance search)"
      - term: United Arab Emirates
      - definition:
        - text: In the UAE, the Emirates Drug Establishment (EDE) has held medicines registration since Federal Decree-Law 28/2023, and the medicines law is Federal Decree-Law 38 of 2024. An ingredient and product-name search of the EDE register found no registered product containing afamelanotide, and none named Scenesse (25 September 2026).
        - generic: "Source: Federal Decree-Law No. (28) of 2023 On the Establishment of the UAE Drug Corporation (official English translation) · Federal Decree-Law No. (38) of 2024 Governing Medical Products, Pharmacists and Pharmaceutical Establishments (official English translation) · Registered medical product directory (Drug Directory)"
      - term: Saudi Arabia
      - definition: "Saudi context: do not conflate afamelanotide (Scenesse) with Melanotan II. Saudi registration or a specific access pathway for Scenesse has not been verified here; foreign approval does not establish its local status."
    - paragraph: Afamelanotide and Melanotan II are both synthetic relatives of α-MSH. Compare them register by register and the resemblance ends at the receptor.
    - strong: Mechanism
    - generic: "Afamelanotide: MC1R agonist · Melanotan II: non-selective"
    - generic: Melanotan II also acts on MC3R, MC4R and MC5R and reaches the brain
    - strong: Human evidence
    - generic: "Afamelanotide: A, for EPP only · Melanotan II: D"
    - generic: Two phase 3 trials in erythropoietic protoporphyria, against a three-volunteer pilot and a ten-man erectile-dysfunction study from the 1990s. The Peptide Pocket Guide rates Melanotan II C and the Aesthetic & Regenerative Endocrinology guide D; with no trial of tanning, this course uses D.
    - strong: Regulatory status
    - generic: "Afamelanotide: EU 2014, US 2019 · Melanotan II: none"
    - generic: Afamelanotide is approved only for EPP, as the manufacturer's implant. Melanotan II is approved for no indication anywhere.
    - strong: Open question
    - generic: Uses beyond EPP; melanoma risk
    - generic: A phase 3 trial of afamelanotide in vitiligo began in 2023 and has posted no results. Whether Melanotan II causes melanoma is unproven.
    - paragraph: A shared receptor does not bring a shared approval.
